summary: Mount Blue, Franklin County, Maine: 47-foot steel lookout from 1931 or 1932, scrapped in 2011, replaced in 2012 by a public radio tower styled as a fire lookout.

facts.design: 47-foot steel lookout tower, removed 2011; replaced by a radio tower built to look like a forest fire tower, with a public observation platform
facts.status_note: The original steel lookout was removed in 2011; a radio tower styled as a fire lookout stands on the summit in its place
facts.agency: Maine Department of Conservation (runs Mt. Blue State Park); Maine Office of Information Technology sponsored the radio project

access.note: The observation deck on the 2012 tower is open to the public by steel steps; the antenna cab is closed to the public

visit.trail_note: About 1.6 miles from the end of the Mount Blue Road, inside Mount Blue State Park

events.note: Annual report says a lookout was erected on Mt. Blue in the fall 1931 program for districts without one; a 2021 Sun Journal list gives 1932
Roof repairs to the lookout cabin, per the 1943-44 biennial report
Old steel remains removed in early September 2011 while the replacement was built; two sections had no takers and were to be sent to scrap
New radio tower built to look like a fire lookout finished on the summit in July 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1931 annual report says a lookout was erected on Mt. Blue in the fall 1931 program; a 2021 Sun Journal list gives 1932. The story reports both and does not pick one.

The 2011 Maine report places Mount Blue in Avon, and Wikipedia places the summit in Avon; the 2012 Maine report, the Sun Journal list and the Daily Bulldog place the summit in Weld, inside Mount Blue State Park. The story gives both placements and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2011 and 2012 events are confirmed by the 2011 and 2012 Maine reports. Erection year conflicts: the 1931 report describes a fall 1931 program; the 2021 Sun Journal list gives 1932; a Facebook caption seen only in search results (not fetched, not cited) also says 1932. A Facebook caption also says the old tower closed at the end of 1971; unverified, left out. No staffing source found. Wikipedia is undated. The 2011 'Avon' mention is a single report; Wikipedia also places the summit in Avon, and the story says so. No photos added.
